title: A Scale of Liking: kedvel, szeret, imád, utál

sections.title: More than just like and don't like
sections.content: Hungarian has a full scale beyond szeret/nem szeret: kedvel (a mild "to like, to be fond of"), szeret (the everyday "to like/to love"), imád (a strong "to adore"), and utál ("to hate"). All four take a plain accusative object when what's liked (or hated) is a thing, not an infinitive.

sections.title: The scale
rows: to like, to be fond of

items.english: I hate it when I'm bored.

sections.content: Unlike érdekel, here the person doing the liking is the ordinary subject, and the verb takes definite conjugation when the object is specific: imádom a focit ("I adore [THE] football") uses -om because a focit is a defined thing, the same rule you already know from other definite-object sentences.
